metadata.title: Write with AI, Still Sound Like You

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. AI writing tools will draft anything you ask for. But if you have ever read what comes back and thought, that does not sound like me, you are not alone. The real question is not how you make the AI write better. It is how you make it sound like you.

backspaces 'write better' → 'sound like me' on the spoken correction

beats.narration_text: Three terms you will need. Voice: the way you sound on the page — your words, your rhythm. A prompt: the instruction you type before the AI writes anything. And a draft: a rough version that nobody is supposed to see.

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Here is the problem. Most people type a prompt, take the first draft, and ship it. And every first draft comes out in the same voice — the AI's default voice. Polite, padded, a little bit robotic. It sounds like everyone. Which means it sounds like no one.

shot.visual_intent: A dark AI block prints pages; three identical pages drop out in a row, all in the same grey voice; the words 'default voice' sit beside them.
shot.motion_claim: A dark AI block prints pages; three identical pages drop out in a row, all in the same grey voice; the words 'default voice' sit beside them.

beats.narration_text: Why does that happen? Because the AI has nothing to copy. A draft is a guess, and with no sample of how you write, the AI falls back on its safest habit — the voice it learned from reading everything. And 'everything' is exactly what makes it sound like everyone.

shot.visual_intent: The same AI block with an empty input tray labelled 'no sample'; identical pages still roll out of it.

show.event: empty tray drops onto the block

shot.motion_claim: The same AI block with an empty input tray labelled 'no sample'; identical pages still roll out of it.

beats.narration_text: Fix one. Give it something to copy. Take one email or paragraph you actually wrote — one that sounds like you — paste it into your prompt, and add the words: match this voice. Now the AI has your words, your rhythm, your sentence length. It is copying you now, not the internet.

shot.visual_intent: A white page labelled 'your email' slides into the AI block; a fresh page comes out carrying a terracotta check and the words 'sounds like you'.
shot.motion_claim: A white page labelled 'your email' slides into the AI block; a fresh page comes out carrying a terracotta check and the words 'sounds like you'.

beats.narration_text: Fix two. Ban the giveaways. AI drafts lean on the same telltale phrases — delve, in today's fast-paced world, and a forest of em-dashes. None of them are wrong. They are just the uniform. Add one line to your prompt: never use these words. The draft comes back plainer. Which is to say, more like a person.

shot.visual_intent: A page lists 'delve', "in today's fast-paced world" and a row of em-dashes; each is crossed out in turn; 'the giveaways' beside.
shot.motion_claim: A page lists 'delve', "in today's fast-paced world" and a row of em-dashes; each is crossed out in turn; 'the giveaways' beside.

beats.narration_text: Fix three. Stop starting from nothing. Instead of asking the AI to invent your thoughts, dictate your rough ones — talk it out, typos and all — and ask it to clean them up. It is easier to keep your ideas and borrow its sentences than to inject your ideas into its sentences.

shot.visual_intent: A speech bubble labelled 'rough thoughts' holds messy scribbled lines; a clean page drops beside it labelled 'cleaned up'.
shot.motion_claim: A speech bubble labelled 'rough thoughts' holds messy scribbled lines; a clean page drops beside it labelled 'cleaned up'.

beats.narration_text: Fix four. Do the last pass yourself. Read the draft out loud, and anywhere it does not sound like something you would say, change it in your own words. The AI did the typing. But the voice at the end — that has to be yours.

shot.visual_intent: A page with three lines; a pencil ellipse circles the middle line, which is swapped for a plainer one; a terracotta check lands; 'your pass' beside.

beats.narration_text: Now watch all four fixes on a real email. The default draft says: I hope this email finds you well. Delving into our proposal dash dash. Nobody talks like that. The fixed version says: Hi Maya, here is the proposal. Page three has the price. Shout if anything looks off. Same facts. One of them sounds like a person.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Here is a paragraph I wrote: [paste it]. Match this voice — my words, my rhythm, my sentence length. Never use these words: delve, leverage, game-changer, in today's fast-paced world. No em-dashes. Below are my rough thoughts, dictated. Clean them up without adding new ideas: [paste your thoughts]. Then check two things yourself. Read it out loud — does it sound like something you would actually say? And did you do your own final pass, in your own words?
